models.notes: AbstractModel with _auto = False (no DB table). Only field is id = fields.Id() so the web client can initialize a dummy form record via onchange(). create() is overridden to a no-op returning self.

security.notes: Single ACL access_board_board_all on model_board_board for base.group_user (read only: perm_read=1, write/create/unlink=0). The model is virtual; per-user customization is persisted in ir.ui.view.custom rows keyed by user_id.

behavioral_notes.observation: board.board is a virtual model: _auto = False means no SQL table is created, and the only field is id = fields.Id(), present solely so the web client can initialize a dummy form record via onchange() when it opens the dashboard. create() is overridden to a no-op (@api.model_create_multi returning self), so nothing is ever persisted to the model itself. The dashboard has no business record of its own — it is a form-view shell. This is invisible to row-count/schema metadata because the model deliberately has no table.

get_view() overrides the ORM view loader: it calls super().get_view() then searches ir.ui.view.custom (sudo) for a row matching (user_id = env.uid, ref_id = view_id). If found, it swaps res['arch'] for the user's saved custom arch and returns custom_view_id. Each user therefore sees their OWN dashboard arch, stored as an ir.ui.view.custom record, not the shared base view. The arch is then run through _arch_preprocessing(), which (a) sets js_class='board' on the root node so the web client instantiates a BoardController instead of a plain FormController, and (b) strips any <action> children that are invisible/unauthorized. None of this per-user view rewriting is visible in static model metadata.

The add_to_dashboard controller is the pinning mechanism. It resolves the 'board.open_board_my_dash_action' xmlid, loads the current user's board arch via board.board.get_view(), finds the first <board>/<column>, and inserts a new <action> element carrying name=action_id, string=name, view_mode, context (allowed_company_ids stripped so multi-company filtering still works on the dashboard) and domain. It then writes the serialized arch into a NEW ir.ui.view.custom row (user_id=session.uid, ref_id=view_id). Effect: any list/pivot/graph/etc. view the user is looking at becomes a saved widget on their personal dashboard. The saved unit is the action reference + its search context/domain, re-resolved live at render time — not a snapshot of data.

behavioral_notes.element: BoardController + BoardAction (OWL rendering of saved widgets)
behavioral_notes.observation: At render time BoardArchParser (board_view.js) walks the saved arch into {layout, columns:[{actions:[...]}]}, where each <action> becomes a widget descriptor (actionId, viewMode, context, domain, isFolded). BoardController (board_controller.js) lays out the columns and, for each descriptor, mounts a BoardAction (board_action.js) which calls rpc('/web/action/load', {action_id}) and embeds a full <View> (list/pivot/graph/...) with controlPanel hidden, re-fetching live data through the standard view stack. So each dashboard cell is a live mini-view, not a cached image.

behavioral_notes.element: Dashboard layout / drag-and-reorder UI (gap #3, OWL/JS in static/src)
behavioral_notes.observation: The interactive dashboard behaviour lives entirely in OWL/JS under static/src and is invisible to Python metadata (metadata gap #3): useSortable in BoardController gives drag-and-drop of widgets within and across columns (moveAction), selectLayout switches column layouts (e.g. '2-1', '1-1-1'), toggleAction folds/unfolds widgets, and closeAction removes one. Every mutation calls saveBoard(), which re-renders the 'board.arch' QWeb template to XML and POSTs it to /web/view/edit_custom (custom_id = customViewId) to persist the user's ir.ui.view.custom arch, then fires an rpcBus 'CLEAR-CACHES'. AddToBoard registers an 'add-to-board' item in the cogMenu registry, shown only for ir.actions.act_window actions whose viewType is not 'form'.

it_architecture.application: board (My Dashboard framework — virtual form-view shell + OWL dashboard widget host, layered on web/spreadsheet_dashboard)
software_services: /board/add_to_dashboard (pin current action/view+context as a dashboard widget)
/web/action/load (reused by BoardAction to load each pinned widget's action)
/web/view/edit_custom (reused by saveBoard to persist per-user dashboard arch)
logical_data_erm: saved <action> name -> ir.actions.act_window (the pinned action, resolved live)
information_flows: pin: user view -> AddToBoard cogMenu -> /board/add_to_dashboard -> board.board.get_view -> create ir.ui.view.custom(user_id, ref_id, arch)

render: open My Dashboard -> board.board.get_view (swap in user's custom arch) -> _arch_preprocessing sets js_class='board' -> BoardController -> per-widget BoardAction -> /web/action/load -> live View
edit: drag/layout/fold/remove (BoardController) -> saveBoard -> /web/view/edit_custom -> update ir.ui.view.custom.arch -> rpcBus CLEAR-CACHES
extends: ir.ui.view.custom (per-user view storage), cogMenu registry, views registry ('board')
frontend_components: BoardController (OWL dashboard root; useSortable drag-and-drop, layout/fold/remove, saveBoard)
BoardAction (one live embedded View per pinned widget; loads action via /web/action/load)
AddToBoard (cogMenu item to pin the current view+context to the dashboard)
BoardArchParser (parses saved board arch into columns/actions descriptors)

capabilities: Compose a personal dashboard from pinned views/actions (self-service)
Pin any non-form act_window view (list/pivot/graph/...) with its search context and domain as a widget
Arrange dashboard widgets (multi-column layout, drag-and-drop, fold, remove)
Render saved widgets as live mini-views (data re-fetched at view time, not snapshotted)
Persist each user's dashboard independently (per-user custom view arch)
value_streams: Pin-to-Dashboard: user opens a view -> Add to my dashboard -> action+context saved as widget in ir.ui.view.custom
Open-to-Render: open My Dashboard -> load user's custom arch -> mount BoardController -> per-widget live View render
information_concepts: ir.ui.view.custom (per-user saved dashboard arch — not owned by board, but the actual persistence)
pinned <action> widget (action ref + view_mode + context + domain)
organization: base.group_user (every internal user has read access to board.board)
policies: ACL grants read-only on board.board to base.group_user (no write/create/unlink on the model itself)
get_view scopes the custom arch to the current user (user_id = env.uid), so dashboards are strictly personal
_arch_preprocessing strips invisible/unauthorized <action> children before rendering (security trimming)
allowed_company_ids is removed from the saved context so multi-company filtering still applies on the dashboard
stakeholders: End user (builds and views their own dashboard)
Module developer (registers views or actions a user may pin)
System administrator (relies on web/spreadsheet_dashboard infrastructure board sits on)

classification.rationale: board is a personal-productivity UI framework, not a business object of its own — Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support' and Porter support activity (firm IT infrastructure). The substance is FRONTEND (gap #3): 4 JS files / 3 QWeb templates implementing the OWL dashboard (BoardController drag/layout/fold, BoardAction live widgets, AddToBoard cogMenu), wrapped around a single virtual model (board.board, _auto=False, no table, one id field) and exactly one route (/board/add_to_dashboard). It owns no data — persistence is delegated to ir.ui.view.custom per user — and depends on spreadsheet_dashboard/web for everything underneath it. activity_class=support because it creates no primary value-chain output; it is cross-cutting tooling every app reuses. APQC 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' is chosen because board's purpose is personal performance/management dashboards — surfacing each user's own KPIs and views (it sits under the Spreadsheet Dashboards menu and lets users assemble their own management view of any data), which maps to 13.0's capability-development / performance-management intent rather than to building or running an IT platform. 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' was considered (board is technical UI plumbing like web) but rejected: unlike web (a concrete runtime/application platform = IT delivery), board delivers no IT service of its own — it is a thin self-service capability that lets business users compose their personal performance dashboards, which is squarely the performance-/capability-management intent of 13.0.

standard_capabilities: Per-user 'My Dashboard' assembled from pinned views
'Add to my dashboard' cog-menu action on any non-form act_window view, capturing its search context + domain
Multi-column dashboard layouts (e.g. 2-1, 1-1-1) with drag-and-drop reordering across columns
Widgets render as live embedded views (list/pivot/graph/kanban/...) re-fetching current data
Strictly personal persistence via ir.ui.view.custom (no admin setup per user)
typical_fits: Power users building a personal KPI/working-set dashboard from existing reports
Pinning a filtered+grouped list or a pivot/graph as a recurring at-a-glance widget
Lightweight personal alternative to building a dedicated dashboard view or spreadsheet
common_gaps: Shared/team dashboards — board dashboards are per-user only (no sharing/publishing)
Bespoke widget types or interactivity beyond embedding an existing view (requires OWL/JS dev, gap #3)
Cross-record analytics/computed KPIs not expressible as a single act_window view (use spreadsheet_dashboard instead)
Pinning form views or non-act_window actions (AddToBoard is gated to act_window, viewType != form)

open_questions: Interaction with spreadsheet_dashboard: board now depends on it and shares its menu root — how far the two dashboard frameworks overlap vs. complement is not evident from board's own code.
Garbage collection of ir.ui.view.custom rows when a pinned action is deleted or a user is removed (board only ever creates rows).
Whether _arch_preprocessing's invisible-<action> stripping fully enforces record-level access of the pinned actions at render time.
